title: Amdahl's Law and the Ceiling on Parallel Speedup
explainer: Performance and cost engineering at scale runs into a limit Gene Amdahl formalized in 1967: the speedup available from parallelizing a workload is capped by whatever fraction of the work must still run sequentially, no matter how many processors or nodes are added. This is why adding more compute to a bottlenecked pipeline often yields diminishing cost-per-throughput returns, and why shrinking the serial portion of a system matters more than raw horizontal scaling. It gives a concrete mathematical basis for the engineering intuition that scaling out has limits.
